Priyom,

Thanks for the call last week. Our legal team sent a first pass with a few asks attached (Novagrid_Redlines_v1.pdf). High level: Novagrid needs clarity on whether the Order Form/MSA grants Redwood any title or assignment in customer content or model outputs, and we want explicit limits on downstream productization of outputs that embed customer trademarks or PII.

Also flagged: training/feedback license language — we need to understand if Novagrid data (including prompts and aggregated telemetry) could ever be used to fine-tune models that might be re‑sold or surfaced to other customers. If that is possible, we need either an opt‑out or stronger anonymization/handback commitments.

We've proposed a couple of alternative clauses in the PDF, but would prefer to work through a short mutual action plan rather than a long redline dance. Can we get a concise response and a proposed timeline for final terms? Procurement hopes to be signed by 11/20 if we can resolve IP/training points.

Tim

Timothy — thanks for sending and for the clear summary. We've pulled in Monica on Sales Ops for procurement timing and Laura from Legal to review the specific phrasing. Initial reactions below; Laura, please weigh in with definitive legal language.

Quick bullets so procurement knows where we stand:
- Output ownership: Redwood's standard position is that customers retain ownership of their input data and any customer‑created output; Redwood requests the right to use de‑identified aggregate telemetry for service improvement only. We're open to tightening language around downstream "productization" where output is repackaged as a competing product.
- Training/feedback license: we can offer an opt‑out for fine‑tuning on a per‑environment basis (Order Form checkbox / exhibit). If Novagrid opts out, Redwood will not use their unredacted prompts or outputs to train models; we can still use aggregated signals for safety/metrics unless Novagrid buys a dedicated private deployment.
- Telemetry & PII: propose explicit commitment to not retain PII in training sets and a retention window for telemetry evidence (30 days raw logs / 1 year aggregated metrics) — legal to confirm specifics.

Next steps: Laura, can you propose redline language for (1) an explicit productization carveout when outputs incorporate customer IP/trademarks, (2) the training opt‑out Exhibit A, and (3) telemetry retention/PII language? Monica — once Laura sends, I can share a short MOP (mutual action plan) with Novagrid and a DocuSign link to an updated Order Form.

Thanks — Priyom

Priyom / Monica — I reviewed Novagrid's PDF and drafted a redline with three focused edits that I think address their concerns while keeping Redwood's operational needs intact. Attached: redline_MSA_novagrid.docx. Summary of proposed language below — this is concise so Sales can present it as a clear choice to Novagrid: 

1) Productization carveout (short): 
   - "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Content and any Outputs containing Customer Content; Redwood shall not market, sell, or otherwise commercialize Outputs that are substantially derived from Customer Content if such Outputs would enable a competing product to Customer. Redwood may use Outputs for benchmarking, safety, and quality improvements in anonymized/aggregated form."

2) Training opt‑out exhibit (Exhibit B): 
   - "Customer may elect, by checking Exhibit B on the Order Form, to opt‑out of Redwood using Customer Content or Outputs for model training or fine‑tuning. If elected, Redwood will not use unredacted prompts, inputs, or outputs for model training; Redwood may retain telemetry and aggregated metrics solely for service stability and security, subject to the PII exclusions below. Election of the opt‑out may be tied to different pricing or service feature availability as set forth in the Order Form."

3) Telemetry & PII: 
   - "Redwood will not retain PII for training purposes; raw request logs containing PII will be deleted within 30 days. Aggregated, non‑identifiable telemetry may be retained for analysis and product improvement for up to 12 months. Redwood will implement commercially reasonable controls to detect and scrub PII prior to any use in model improvement processes."

I included alternative tighter wording for the productization sentence (two variants) so Novagrid can choose stricter or looser language. The redline.docx includes tracked changes and a short comment thread. If Sales wants a faster path we can accept the opt‑out and offer a 5% uplift or addendum that limits some new features until an opt‑out customer migrates to Redwood Dedicated.

Happy to hop on a 20‑minute call with Novagrid legal if that accelerates resolution.

—Laura
